info.title: agency
info.summary: Run and converse with the `agency` agent harness over HTTP.
info.description:
HTTP surface for the `agency` harness.

Every endpoint runs the same code path as the CLI: options are built by
`agency.options.build_options`, so a run over HTTP and a run from `agency run` are
configured identically. Errors are [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457)
problem documents.

200.description: The completed run, including its tool and delegation trace.

get.summary: List the agents this server can invoke

200.description: The subagent roster: each agent's model, tools and turn cap, plus its live status in this process.

get.description:
One roster entry, resolved by id.

Same data and same status source as the collection, so a client can poll a single
agent without pulling and filtering the whole roster.

404, not an empty 200: an unknown id is a caller error -- a stale name pinned in a
config, or a typo -- and returning a body for it would let that error survive as far
as `POST /v1/runs`, where it fails much less legibly. The bound on `agent_id` keeps
a junk path segment out of the error body; over it, the 422 is the honest answer,
since no agent name is 64 characters long.

parameters.name: agent_id

schema.description: The agent's `id` from `GET /v1/agents` (equal to its name today).
schema.title: Agent Id

parameters.description: The agent's `id` from `GET /v1/agents` (equal to its name today).

200.description: The agent's model, tools, turn cap and availability, plus its live status in this process.

get.description:
What this process is holding open, oldest first.

Per-process, like `GET /v1/agents`' status: sessions are local subprocesses, so with
more than one uvicorn worker each worker lists only its own. It is an operational
view -- "what is this box holding" -- not a user's conversation history.

200.description: Every session this process currently holds open.

404.description: No such session; it was closed or expired

post.description:
Connect a session and hold it open.

201, not 200: this creates a server-side resource -- a live SDK subprocess -- that
the caller is now responsible for closing. `expires_at` in the body is the safety
net if they do not.

The profile is resolved here rather than in the store, so what comes back names the
profile the session is actually running, not `null` meaning "whatever the server
was configured with at the time".

201.description: The new session. Send messages to it, then close it.

404.description: No such session; it was closed or expired

get.description:
Poll one session. `status` is what a client waits on before sending a turn, and
a 404 is the honest answer for a handle that has expired -- see `SessionStore.get`.

200.description: The session's status, turn count and expiry.

404.description: No such session; it was closed or expired

delete.description:
Release the subprocess and the context.

Refuses while a turn is in flight rather than tearing the client out from under it:
that would surface to the caller mid-turn as a 502 with no explanation. The wait is
bounded by the turn's own timeout, and a client that has given up entirely does not
need this endpoint at all -- the idle reaper collects the session either way.

204 and idempotent-ish: a `DELETE` of an id that has already been closed or reaped
is a 404 from `sessions.get`, which is the truthful answer to "is this handle live".

404.description: No such session; it was closed or expired

409.description: A turn is in flight; wait for it to finish

post.summary: Send one message and get the reply
post.description:
One turn of the conversation.

A turn takes a `RunSlots` slot as well as the session lock. An open session is idle
weight -- a subprocess and some memory -- but a *running* turn is exactly as
expensive as a `POST /v1/runs`, so the two endpoints share one bound on concurrent
model work. Without that, N sessions would be N ways around the run cap.

`is_error=True` inside `run` is still a 200, same contract as `POST /v1/runs`. What
differs is the failure handling: a timeout or a transport error cancels the drain
mid-stream and leaves the SDK client in an indeterminate state, so `SessionStore`
closes the session on the way out. The 504 and 502 bodies say so, because "retry the
same session id" would otherwise be the obvious and wrong next move.

200.description: The completed turn, including its tool and delegation trace.

404.description: No such session; it was closed or expired

409.description: A turn is already in flight on this session

502.description: The agent loop failed; the session was closed

get.description:
The audit trail for one pack.

This is what replaces `git log` once the database is authoritative: every edit is a
new immutable revision, and a completed run names the revision id it held.

put.summary: Create a pack, or add a revision to one
put.description:
Idempotent on content: identical content does not mint a revision.

PUT rather than PATCH because a revision is whole -- there is no partial edit of an
immutable row, and offering one would suggest the previous content is still in play.

422.description: The pack could never be honoured

delete.description:
Archive, never delete. `run_grant` rows reference a pack forever, and a run whose
capability vanished is a run nobody can explain.

post.summary: Write the in-code seed registry into the database

get.description: Assignments applied to every matching run before the caller asks for anything.

delete.description: Disables rather than deletes, so the history of what was once granted survives.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable identity. Equal to `name` today; it exists separately so a worker can be renamed without breaking clients that key off it.

name.title: Name
name.description: Key the manager invokes this agent by, e.g. 'reviewer'.

status.description: Live state in THIS server process, from the subagent hook stream. Runs are in-process, so an agent reads `running` only while this server is actually invoking it -- with uvicorn --workers N each worker reports its own view.

description.title: Description
description.description: When the agent should be used. This is what drives the model's routing.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model alias ('sonnet', 'opus', ...) or full ID. None inherits the run's.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Tools the agent may use. None means it inherits the main thread's set.

max_turns.title: Max Turns
max_turns.description: Turn cap for one invocation. None means the run's default applies.

availability.title: Availability
availability.description: 'always' -- loaded on every run. 'team' -- only present when the run is started with team=<name>; see the `team` field for which one.

team.title: Team
team.description: Name of the team this worker belongs to, or null for an always-available agent. Pass this as `team` on POST /v1/runs or POST /v1/sessions to reach it.

grantable.title: Grantable
grantable.description: Capability packs this agent may hold. Pass one under `grants.agents` on a run or session request.

barred.title: Barred
barred.description: Packs this agent may never hold, because a ceiling forbids a tool they contain. Named explicitly so a refusal is discoverable before it happens rather than arriving as an apparently arbitrary 422.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: UTC time this agent entered its current status. Never null: an agent that has not run reports the time this server started observing, because it has genuinely been idle since then. Use `invocations == 0` to tell 'never ran' from 'ran and finished' -- do not infer it from the timestamp. Not a definition timestamp: editing team.py does not move it.

invocations.title: Invocations
invocations.description: Times this agent has been started in this process. Resets on restart.

AgentInfo.title: AgentInfo
AgentInfo.description:
One subagent the server can invoke.

Deliberately not the whole `AgentDefinition`: `prompt` is the agent's system prompt
and is an implementation detail, not a wire contract -- publishing it would make
every prompt tweak a breaking API change. What is here is what a caller needs to
choose an agent and predict what it can do.

AgentStatus.title: AgentStatus
AgentStatus.description:
The app renders one pill per value. Adding a member is a breaking change
for any client that has not shipped support for it — which is the whole
point of it being an enum in the spec rather than a free string.

`(str, Enum)` rather than `enum.StrEnum`: StrEnum is 3.11+, and this project
declares `requires-python = ">=3.10"`. On 3.10 the import alone raises and takes
the whole API down with it. The two serialise identically here.

Not every member is reachable today. What the SDK hook stream can actually tell us
is start, stop and delegation failure, which yields `idle`, `running` and `error`.
`starting`, `paused` and `stopped` are reserved -- kept because removing a member is
as breaking as adding one, but nothing emits them:

- `starting` would have to come from the `Agent` PreToolUse, which also fires for
  calls the guardrail then denies. There is no matching event on the deny path, so
  the count would leak and wedge an agent in `starting` forever. Left unemitted
  rather than shipped wedge-prone.
- `paused` / `stopped` have no source at all: the SDK exposes `interrupt()` on the
  main session, not on individual workers, so a worker is never paused or stopped
  as a distinct state -- it is running or it is gone.

count.title: Count
count.description: Length of `agents`. Redundant on purpose -- it saves clients a scan.

AgentsResponse.title: AgentsResponse
AgentsResponse.description:
Body of `GET /v1/agents`: the subagent roster.

Only subagents are listed. The manager is not one -- it is the main thread agent you
talk to, so it has no name to invoke and nothing to discover; `team=<name>` on
`POST /v1/runs` is what selects it and its workers. See `agents/team.py`.

Kept an envelope rather than a bare array so fields can be added without breaking
clients, and because a top-level JSON array is awkward to extend.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Team name for 'team', agent name for 'agent', null for 'lead'.

AssignmentInfo.title: AssignmentInfo
AssignmentInfo.description: One standing grant: applied to every matching run, before the caller asks.

source.title: Source
source.description: 'database' or 'seed'. Worth publishing: the two are edited very differently -- one through this API, the other by shipping a commit.

CapabilitiesResponse.title: CapabilitiesResponse
CapabilitiesResponse.description:
Body of `GET /v1/capabilities`. An envelope, for the same reason `AgentsResponse`
is one: a bare array cannot grow a field.

CapabilityHistoryResponse.title: CapabilityHistoryResponse
CapabilityHistoryResponse.description: Every revision of one pack, oldest first.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the pack is for. This is what a human reads when approving it.

prompt_note.title: Prompt Note
prompt_note.description: Appended to the grantee's prompt. A tool a worker was never told it has is a tool it will not use.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: 1-based. 0 means this came from the in-code seed, not the database.

revision_id.title: Revision Id
revision_id.description: Database id of this exact content. Pinned on every run that held the pack, which is what keeps a completed run explicable after a later edit.

CapabilityInfo.title: CapabilityInfo
CapabilityInfo.description: One pack, at a given revision.

description.title: Description
description.description: Mandatory. A capability nobody can explain is one nobody should approve.

mcp_servers.title: Mcp Servers
mcp_servers.description: Must already be loaded by this server. A pack may scope a worker to an existing MCP server; it may not introduce one.

CapabilityWrite.title: CapabilityWrite
CapabilityWrite.description:
Body of `POST`/`PUT /v1/capabilities`.

No `revision` field: revisions are minted, never chosen. A caller that could pick one
could overwrite history, which is the property this whole table exists to prevent.

lead.title: Lead
lead.description: Packs for the main thread -- the manager in team mode, else the agent.

team.title: Team
team.description: Packs for every worker of the selected team. A worker whose ceiling forbids a pack is skipped rather than failing the run; see `skipped_grants` on the response.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Packs for one named agent. Unlike `team`, a ceiling violation here is a 422 -- you named the agent, so a silent drop would hide your mistake.

GrantsModel.title: GrantsModel
GrantsModel.description:
Capability packs to attach to this run, by scope.

Names only. A free-form tool list here would be simpler and strictly worse: it moves
the security decision from a reviewed registry to the call site, it cannot carry the
prompt note that makes a granted tool actually get used, and it makes
`GET /v1/capabilities` meaningless.

Health.title: Health
Health.description:
Liveness. Cheap and dependency-free by design -- a liveness probe that checks
dependencies restarts the process when a dependency blips, which is backwards.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: The next turn of the conversation.

MessageRequest.title: MessageRequest
MessageRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/messages`.

Only a prompt. `profile` and `team` are absent on purpose and, because of
`extra="forbid"`, sending either is a 422 rather than a silent no-op: they were
baked into the `ClaudeAgentOptions` this session connected with, so there is no
honest way to honour them mid-conversation. Open a new session instead.

turn.title: Turn
turn.description: 1-based index of this turn within the session. `run.run_id` is per-turn.

MessageResponse.title: MessageResponse
MessageResponse.description:
Result of one turn.

The turn's result is nested as `run` rather than flattened alongside `session_id`,
so it is the *same* object `POST /v1/runs` returns -- a client can render a turn and
a one-shot run with one code path, and a field added to `RunResponse` cannot collide
with a session field.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem document. Declared so it shows up in the OpenAPI schema; the
responses themselves are built in `errors.py`.

Readiness.title: Readiness
Readiness.description: Readiness. Checks the things a run actually needs before accepting traffic.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Cross-worker note: this reloads THIS process only. Other workers pick the change up within AGENCY_CAPABILITY_CACHE_TTL_S.

ReloadResponse.title: ReloadResponse
ReloadResponse.description: Result of dropping the registry cache.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Override the server's configured profile for this run.

team.title: Team
team.description: Name of a team from agents/team.py to run as manager+workers instead of the solo agent, e.g. 'engineering'. Omit or null for a solo agent. See GET /v1/agents for the current roster, grouped by team.

grants.description: Capability packs to attach. Omit for the agent's default powers. See GET /v1/capabilities for what exists and which agents may hold each pack.

grants.title: Grants
grants.description: Capability packs this run actually held, keyed by scope ('lead', 'team:<agent>', 'agent:<agent>'). Echoed rather than reflected back from the request: a team-scoped pack a worker's ceiling refused does not appear here.

skipped_grants.title: Skipped Grants
skipped_grants.description: Team-scoped packs a worker's ceiling declined, with the reason. Empty on almost every run; when it is not, this is the difference between what you asked for and what ran.

RunResponse.title: RunResponse
RunResponse.description:
Result of a completed run. `is_error=True` is still a 200: the request
succeeded, the agent did not. Transport failures get a 5xx problem instead.

written.title: Written
written.description: Packs that produced a new revision. Empty is normal.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Pin the profile for the whole session. Fixed at open time.

team.title: Team
team.description: Name of a team from agents/team.py to open the session as, instead of the solo agent, e.g. 'engineering'. Omit or null for a solo agent. Fixed at open time -- see MessageRequest.

grants.description: Capability packs to attach. Omit for the agent's default powers. See GET /v1/capabilities for what exists and which agents may hold each pack.

SessionCreateRequest.title: SessionCreateRequest
SessionCreateRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/sessions`. Every field is optional: the server's own profile
and a solo (non-team) agent are the defaults, same as `POST /v1/runs`.

id.title: Id
id.description: Opaque handle. Mint it here; do not construct one.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Profile the session connected with. Fixed for its life.

team.title: Team
team.description: Team this session runs as manager+workers, or null for a solo agent.

status.title: Status
status.description: 'busy' while a turn is in flight. A message sent to a busy session is a 409, not a queued turn.

turns.title: Turns
turns.description: Messages completed in this session so far.

last_active_at.title: Last Active At
last_active_at.description: When the last turn finished. What the idle TTL is measured from.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the server may reap this session for idleness. Null when the TTL is disabled. A floor, not a promise: reaping happens on request, so a session may outlive it on an idle server.

SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo
SessionInfo.description:
One open session. Deliberately not the conversation itself: the transcript is not
stored here (each turn is persisted as its own run record, keyed by `run_id`), and
the SDK client behind it is not something a client can be handed a view of.

SessionsResponse.title: SessionsResponse
SessionsResponse.description:
Body of `GET /v1/sessions`. An envelope for the same reason `AgentsResponse` is
one: a bare array cannot grow a field.

SkippedGrantInfo.title: SkippedGrantInfo
SkippedGrantInfo.description: A team-scoped pack one worker did not receive, and why.

ToolEvent.title: ToolEvent
ToolEvent.description: One entry of the run's tool trace.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness probes. Never authenticated.

tags.name: agents
tags.description: Agent discovery: which subagents this server can invoke.

tags.name: capabilities
tags.description: Capability packs and standing grants. Reading needs the ordinary API key; changing what agents may do needs a separate admin key, and is disabled unless one is configured.

tags.name: sessions
tags.description: Multi-turn conversations. A session holds a live agent context open across requests; close it when you are done, or it is reaped when idle.
